claims.text: Newborn hearing screen: confirm the initial screen was completed, verify results and follow up as appropriate; newborns should be screened per the Year 2007 Position Statement: Principles and Guidelines for Early Hearing Detection and Intervention Programs.
claims.quote: 8. Confirm initial screen was completed, verify results, and follow up, as appropriate. Newborns should be screened, per "Year 2007 Position Statement: Principles and Guidelines for Early Hearing Detection and Intervention Programs"

claims.text: Hearing: audiometry including 6,000 and 8,000 Hz once between 11 and 14 years, once between 15 and 17 years, and once between 18 and 21 years.
claims.quote: 10. Screen with audiometry including 6,000 and 8,000 Hz high frequencies once between 11 and 14 years, once between 15 and 17 years, and once between 18 and 21 years.

claims.text: Vision: visual acuity screen at ages 4 and 5 years and in cooperative 3-year-olds; instrument-based screening may assess risk at 12 and 24 months, in addition to the 3- through 5-year visits.
claims.quote: 7. A visual acuity screen is recommended at ages 4 and 5 years, as well as in cooperative 3-year-olds. Instrument-based screening may be used to assess risk at ages 12 and 24 months, in addition to the well visits at 3 through 5 years of age.

claims.text: Dental home: check that the child has one; if not, do a risk assessment and refer. Recommend brushing with fluoride toothpaste in the right amount for age.
claims.quote: 35. Assess whether the child has a dental home. If no dental home is identified, perform a risk assessment (https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/oral-health/oral-healthpractice-tools/) and refer to a dental home. Recommend brushing with fluoride toothpaste in the proper dosage for age.
